target.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata
target.body:
## Summary

- Back ACP structured exec approval metadata with a real Gateway request contract instead of parser-only field reads.
- Pass public `exec` tool-call metadata into Gateway-host and Node-host approval registration so production approval requests include the originating title and `toolCallId`.
- Allow `exec.approval.request` to carry optional `title` and `toolCallId`, store sanitized metadata on the pending approval request, and broadcast it through `exec.approval.requested`.
- Add Gateway producer, public exec caller, host registration, ACP translator, and local Gateway e2e regression coverage.
- Regenerate the Swift Gateway protocol model so the new optional approval metadata fields are present in tracked bundled protocol artifacts.

## What Problem This Solves

The previous patch preserved `request.title` and `request.toolCallId` in the ACP parser, but real Gateway `exec.approval.requested` events could not produce those fields because the closed Gateway request schema rejected them and the Gateway request producer did not store or broadcast them.

That made the ACP parser change a test-only contract: ACP appeared to preserve metadata that the live Gateway event path could not send.

This update makes structured `exec.approval.requested` events the source of truth for ACP permission `title` and `toolCallId` by adding the metadata at the public `exec` caller, host approval registration, Gateway schema, request builder, stored payload, producer, and translator/e2e test boundaries.

## User Impact

ACP clients receiving relayed Gateway exec approvals can keep the original tool-call correlation id and user-facing approval title instead of falling back to `exec:<approvalId>` and `Command approval requested` for early structured approval events.

This keeps permission prompts easier to correlate with the originating exec tool call while leaving approval decisions, allowed options, command hydration, and fallback behavior unchanged when metadata is absent.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #79337, which introduced ACP exec approval permission relay support.
- **Gap this fills:** #79337 covered the relay contract and fallback structured approval behavior; this follow-up backs structured approval metadata with the Gateway request/event source before ACP consumes it.
- **Linked issue context:** #3257 is related approval visibility/auditability context, but this PR is a narrower Gateway-to-ACP metadata contract fix and does not claim to close #3257.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- Searched open PRs for `permission-relay toolCallId title`, `exec approval metadata`, `exec.approval.requested title`, and `ACP approval metadata`; no open competing PR was found for the ACP structured exec approval metadata contract.
- #92236 is an open progress/commentary WebChat PR and does not touch ACP exec approval permission relay metadata.
- The linked issue proof prework flagged nonlocal Discord/live channel context for #3257; this PR does not claim Discord or third-party channel proof and scopes the proof to the local Gateway approval event boundary under review.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Structured Gateway exec approval events should carry and relay real `request.title` and `request.toolCallId` into ACP `session/request_permission`, and production public `exec` tool calls should pass the originating tool-call metadata into host approval registration instead of relying on parser-only fields.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw PR worktree on Linux with Node/pnpm. The proof exercises the public `exec` tool caller, Gateway-host and Node-host approval registration paths, the actual Gateway `exec.approval.request` handler, `ExecApprovalManager`, Gateway broadcast payload, `AcpGatewayAgent.handleGatewayEvent`, ACP `request_permission` mapping, a running local Gateway server with a separate operator connection, and the Gateway `exec.approval.resolve` handler.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm test src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts

env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts -t "passes exec tool call metadata"

env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts -t "metadata|forwards prepared systemRunPlan"

env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts

env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree pnpm check:test-types

- **Evidence after fix:**

```

The translator regression starts from a Gateway-produced event, not a hand-built ACP helper payload:

```text
Gateway exec.approval.request params:
  id: approval-gateway-raw
  sessionKey: agent:main:main
  title: Run echo raw
  toolCallId: tool-raw

Observed ACP permission request:
  rawInput.approvalId: approval-gateway-raw
  toolCall.toolCallId: tool-raw
  toolCall.title: Run echo raw

Observed Gateway resolution:
  exec.approval.resolve({ id: approval-gateway-raw, decision: allow-once })
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Gateway accepts optional approval metadata, production public `exec` calls forward the real `toolCallId` and display title into Gateway/Node approval registrations, `exec.approval.requested` broadcasts the metadata, ACP uses it for `request_permission`, and the selected ACP/operator decision resolves the same Gateway approval id.
- **Round 2 CI attribution:** `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` was directly introduced by this PR because the schema change required regenerating the tracked Swift Gateway protocol model. `check-guards`, `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, `check-lint`, and related UI build failures also reported `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` conflict markers, but those were present only in the stale GitHub merge ref based on main commit `632efa2d7343f44408c3e25b1de20e7de889534e`; current PR head and current `origin/main` do not contain those markers, and main later resolved them in `0e3ce24cc8 fix(ui): resolve sidebar merge markers`.
- **What was not tested:** No hosted third-party service, Discord channel, external ACP client UI, or remote CI completion is claimed here. The proof is local and targets the Gateway-to-ACP approval event boundary and production exec caller metadata path that the review findings identified.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause contract fix.

## Maintainer-ready details

- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the Gateway-to-ACP metadata contract under review. The patch derives metadata at the public `exec` caller, carries it through Gateway-host and Node-host approval registration, defines optional metadata at the Gateway protocol schema, stores it on the pending approval payload, broadcasts it in the structured approval event, and verifies ACP consumption from both Gateway-produced tests and a local running Gateway e2e.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** ACP clients can correlate the permission prompt with the original exec tool call and display the intended approval title instead of a synthetic fallback, without changing approval decisions or command execution policy.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR is limited to optional `title` and `toolCallId` metadata on exec approval requests/events and ACP permission relay consumption. It does not change channel transports, Discord proof behavior, provider execution, approval policy, or command resolution.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source of truth is the public `exec` invocation metadata flowing into host approval registration and then into the structured `exec.approval.requested` payload produced from Gateway `record.request`. Because `buildRequestedApprovalEvent(record)` broadcasts that request unchanged, the contract belongs in the public caller, host request builder, `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema`, and `createExecApprovalHandlers` before ACP reads it.
- **Patch quality notes:** The diff is focused on the approval metadata contract, generated Gateway protocol artifacts, and matching tests. The generated Swift model update is the tracked output of `pnpm protocol:gen:swift` after adding optional `title` and `toolCallId` to the Gateway schema.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Addressed by adding optional `title` and `toolCallId` to `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema` instead of keeping a parser-only mapping.
- **RF-002:** Addressed with after-fix proof from Gateway-produced `exec.approval.requested` payloads passed into the ACP translator and resolved through the Gateway handler.
- **RF-003:** Addressed by extending `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts` so translator-level coverage starts from the structured event shape and verifies ACP `request_permission` metadata.
- **RF-004:** Addressed by replacing helper-only proof with Gateway handler → broadcast payload → ACP translator → Gateway resolve proof.
- **RF-005:** Addressed by wiring real production callers: `createExecTool(...).execute(toolCallId, ...)` derives the approval title and forwards the real tool call id through Gateway-host and Node-host approval registration into `exec.approval.request`.
- **RF-006:** Addressed by defining the approval-boundary contract, sanitizing `title` with the existing exec approval display sanitizer before storing/broadcasting it, normalizing `toolCallId` as a non-empty optional string, and regenerating the tracked Swift Gateway protocol model for the schema change.
- **RF-007:** Addressed with the contract-backed production path: public exec caller metadata now reaches the Gateway request contract before ACP consumes it. Maintainer review is still expected for the public approval-boundary decision, but the branch no longer leaves the decision implicit in a parser-only patch.
- **RF-008:** Addressed by backing `src/acp/permission-relay.ts` metadata reads with a real Gateway schema/producer source.
- **RF-009:** Addressed by running the exact requested focused command: `pnpm test src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts`, which passed 4 Vitest shards in 160.54s.
- **RF-010:** Addressed by running `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree pnpm check:test-types`, which completed both core and extensions test typecheck commands.
- **RF-011:** Addressed by running `pnpm lint --threads=8`, which completed the core, extensions, and scripts oxlint shards.
- **RF-012:** Addressed by running the local real Gateway e2e through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts`; the test passed with a running Gateway server, a public exec call, an operator connection observing `exec.approval.requested`, approval resolution, and completed stdout verification.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts` for the running local Gateway server, public exec caller, operator event observation, approval resolution, and completed command output proof.
- **Additional target test files:** `src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts` for the public exec caller metadata regression, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` and `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` for host registration forwarding, `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts` for request payload forwarding, `src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts` for schema/producer coverage, `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts` for Gateway event → ACP translator proof, and `src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts` for parser helper coverage.
- **Scenario locked in:** Public `exec` calls provide `title` and `toolCallId`, host approval registration forwards them into `exec.approval.request`, Gateway broadcasts them in `exec.approval.requested`, ACP uses those values in `request_permission`, and ACP/operator decision resolution still targets the same Gateway approval id.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests cover the caller, host registration, protocol schema, Gateway producer, structured event payload, ACP translator intake, local Gateway e2e boundary, and existing parser helper without launching unrelated channel transports.
- `pnpm test src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts`
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts -t "passes exec tool call metadata"`
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts -t "metadata|forwards prepared systemRunPlan"`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts`
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree pnpm check:test-types`
- `pnpm lint --threads=8`
- `pnpm test:bundled`
- `pnpm protocol:check`

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: 🚨 other` from the parser-only contract drift review.
- **Risk explanation:** This path crosses the exec approval display/permission boundary, so user-facing strings must be schema-backed and sanitized before ACP consumes them.
- **Why acceptable:** The metadata is optional, the existing fallback behavior remains for events that omit it, `title` uses the existing exec approval display sanitizer, `toolCallId` is only accepted as a normalized non-empty string, and approval decision semantics are unchanged. Compatibility risk is limited to adding optional schema fields, availability risk is covered by preserving request registration/resolution behavior, and security-boundary risk is covered by sanitizing display text before ACP consumes it.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low-to-moderate because this adds optional metadata to a public Gateway approval request/event contract. Existing clients that omit `title` or `toolCallId` keep the current fallback behavior, and the closed schema still rejects unrelated extra fields.

The stored approval request payload gains two optional fields only; command text, command preview, command argv, approval visibility, allowed decisions, and resolution behavior are unchanged.

## What was not changed

- Did not change ACP permission option mapping or Gateway approval decision policy.
- Did not change command hydration through `exec.approval.get`.
- Did not change legacy agent approval event parsing.
- Did not add third-party channel, Discord, or hosted provider behavior.
- Did not claim remote CI or external live proof before the updated PR checks run.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `parseGatewayExecApprovalRequestEventPayload` was updated to read `request.title` and `request.toolCallId`, but real public `exec` callers did not pass that metadata into host approval registration, and the Gateway approval request schema/producer did not define or emit those fields. Real structured `exec.approval.requested` events therefore could not satisfy the ACP parser contract.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The metadata is now introduced at the public exec caller, forwarded through host approval registration, accepted by the Gateway request contract and producer, stored in the pending approval payload, broadcast through the existing `buildRequestedApprovalEvent(record)` path, and then consumed by ACP. That fixes the source-of-truth event path rather than adding downstream fallback logic.
